# PROPOSAL — the marker pipeline is four files deep, the bottom one cannot be regenerated by anyone, and 94% of it is overwritten before it reaches the page. It is down to 48 real ports on 7 hulls. Here is what I think we do about it, and the two alternatives.

    from      C1 (Cowork), 2026-08-27
    for       Sleven
    status    PROPOSAL. Nothing changed. This is a decision, not an order.

---

## 1. WHAT THE PAGE ACTUALLY READS TODAY

    LAYER 1   hardpoints_fleet.json          178 hulls   writer: place_fleet.py
                                                         -- NOT IN THIS REPO
    LAYER 2   alignment_overlay.json           7 hulls   the older overlay
    LAYER 3   alignment_overlay_client.json  167 hulls   CIG transforms, CORRECTS layer 1
    LAYER 4   fleet_records_client.json       41 hulls   CIG transforms, ADDS to layer 1

**167 of the 178 base hulls are corrected before they reach the page. That is
94%.** Another 41 hulls never existed in the base at all.

**What is left of layer 1 after the corrections:**

    ATLS                    0 ports      MDC                     0 ports
    ROC                     0 ports      ROC-DS                  0 ports
    MPUV Personnel          1 port       MTC                     1 port
    Nox Kue                 5 ports      Dragonfly Yellowjacket  6 ports
    Glaive                 11 ports      Vanduul Scythe         11 ports
    MISC Starfarer Gemini  13 ports

**Seven hulls with any markers at all, 48 ports between them**, and every one of
those 48 is a name-derived guess sitting a median 0.488 of a half-extent from
the real mount.

## 2. WHY THIS IS A PROBLEM AND NOT JUST UNTIDY

**Rule 14 says one writer per artifact.** The page's markers now have four, and
the one at the bottom — the file that decides *which hulls get markers at all* —
**has a writer that is not in the repository.** `place_fleet.py` cannot be run,
read, or fixed by anybody. That is why the 41 new hulls had to arrive as a
separate additive file in the first place: I could not add a record to the file
that decides records.

**So the base file is frozen, mostly wrong, and load-bearing for exactly 48
ports.** Every future correction has to be another layer on top of it, and each
layer is another place for a hull to be silently missing.

**It also makes the build harder to reason about than it needs to be.** Four
merges in one function, each with its own match-or-die rule, and a reader has to
hold all four to answer "where did this dot come from".

## 3. WHAT I RECOMMEND — make the CIG transforms the base, keep the old file as a
named fallback

One file, one writer, generated from `hardpoint-placement/` in full — every hull
we have transforms for, not just the ones the old file lacked. The old file stops
being the base and becomes an explicitly-named fallback for the handful of hulls
CIG geometry cannot reach.

    hardpoints_from_cig.json     ONE writer (build_hardpoint_overlay.py),
                                 regenerable from Data.p4k by anyone
    hardpoints_fleet.json        FALLBACK ONLY, for the 7 named hulls,
                                 frozen and labelled as un-regenerable

**Why this and not the others:** it is the only option that ends with one writer
and a regenerable artifact, which is what every other data path in this project
already has. It also makes the page's provenance answerable in one sentence —
*these came out of CIG's geometry, except these seven, which are named.*

**The cost, stated plainly:** it changes what `build_deploy.py` reads, so it is
not purely in my lane, and it needs Code to change a merge he owns. And it must
not go in the same week as a release — if it drops a hull, it drops it silently
unless the swap carries a control that counts markers before and after and
refuses on any loss. **That control is the condition of doing it at all.**

## 4. ALTERNATIVE A — leave it, and just document it

Write the layering down, name the 7 hulls, move on.

**For:** zero risk, zero work, nothing can break. The page is correct today.
**Against:** the next person to add a hull hits the same wall I did and invents a
fifth layer. And "94% of this file is overwritten" is the kind of fact that stops
being known the moment the person who measured it stops working on it.

**This is the right answer if the site is going live soon.** It is the wrong
answer if there are months of data work ahead, and there are.

## 5. ALTERNATIVE B — rewrite `place_fleet.py` from scratch

Rebuild the missing writer so the base file is regenerable again.

**For:** restores the original design, no new file, nothing downstream changes.
**Against:** it rebuilds a generator whose output we now overwrite 94% of. **We
would be reconstructing a tool in order to keep producing numbers we throw
away.** The reason the base file exists — that nothing better was available —
stopped being true the day the CIG transforms decoded.

I do not recommend this and I would argue against it.

## 6. WHAT I AM NOT PROPOSING

**Not touching the overlay's per-port correction.** It is proven, it is bounded
by a gate with controls, and it moves 1,720 ports onto CIG's own numbers. Nothing
here changes that mechanism — only which file it writes into.

**Not deleting anything.** The old file stays on disk either way. Seven hulls
still need it.

## 7. THE QUESTION FOR SLEVEN

**Do we spend a session collapsing four layers into one before more data work, or
do we document it and carry on?**

My recommendation is §3, **after** the current check sweep is green and **not**
in the same week as anything else touching the ship page. If the answer is
"later", §4 is honest and I will write the documentation instead.
